_status: From the medical lead's workbook (Master Health Indicator Catalog). Shown in the Learn pop-up; it wins over regions.json / measurements.json text where they disagree (those files are kept unchanged). Re-run backend/scripts/import_medical.py after a new export.

01.name: Heart Rate (HR)
how_to_measure: Don and secure chest strap or smart shirt ensuring direct skin contact over sternum/ribcage.
Power on sensor module and verify Bluetooth/telemetry sync with ISS biomedical laptop/tablet.
Calibrate signal quality, confirm real-time waveform display, and wear continuously during duty/sleep.
01.what: Autonomic nervous system activity, cardiac workload, and cardiovascular function.
01.why_space: Microgravity removes hydrostatic blood pressure gradients, causing fluid headward shift, stroke volume drop, and elevated resting/workload HR.
01.space_effect: Transient resting bradycardia during first 24-48h, followed by compensatory upward shift (+5 to 10 bpm) and blunted peak exercise HR.
01.abnormal: Persistent tachycardia signals dehydration, infection, hypercapnia, or deconditioning; bradycardia indicates excessive vagal tone or conduction defect.
01.baseline: 30-day pre-flight seated resting morning average HR (± 5 bpm).
01.limitations: Motion artifact during physical activity; sensor displacement; dry skin poor PPG conductivity.
01.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Cardiovascular Health & Physiological Monitoring)

02.name: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
02.method: Resting 5-min ECG recording / optical wearable telemetry
how_to_measure: Assume quiet resting seated or supine position for 5 minutes in low-stimulation environment.
Initiate 5-minute timed high-resolution resting ECG/PPG capture sequence via onboard app.
Complete measurement without speaking or shifting position; verify R-R interval data integrity.
02.what: Sympathetic vs parasympathetic autonomic cardiac modulation and baroreceptor responsiveness.
02.why_space: Serves as an objective, sensitive biomarker for accumulated operational stress, neuroendocrine exhaustion, and recovery quality in orbit.
02.space_effect: Depressed rMSSD by 20% to 30% during spaceflight due to continuous sympathetic dominance, sleep fragmentation, and microgravity adaptation.
02.abnormal: Pronounced rMSSD drop indicates acute autonomic strain, elevated allostatic load, fatigue, or operational stress; HRV alone cannot diagnose autonomic collapse.
02.baseline: 14-day pre-flight standardized morning 5-minute seated resting rMSSD baseline.
02.limitations: Highly sensitive to transient emotional state, recent caffeine, circadian timing, and respiration rate.
02.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Autonomic Function & Cardiovascular Monitoring)

03.name: Oxygen Saturation (SpO₂)
03.method: Fingertip pulse oximeter / wearable optical sensor
how_to_measure: Clean and warm index or middle finger; inspect sensor emitter and detector windows.
Apply oximeter probe firmly to fingertip; rest hand motionless on stable surface.
Record continuous SpO2 and pulse reading after signal stabilizes for at least 30 seconds.
03.what: Percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin in arterial blood circulation.
03.why_space: Confirms systemic tissue oxygenation in sealed cabin environments vulnerable to ECLSS fluctuations, pocket hypercapnia, and hypobaric operations.
03.space_effect: Mild transient reduction to 95–97% from cephalad fluid shifts, pulmonary capillary engorgement, and altered ventilation-perfusion matching.
03.abnormal: Desaturation indicates arterial hypoxia, ECLSS scrub failure, toxic inhalation, atelectasis, or acute pulmonary impairment.
03.baseline: Individual pre-flight resting room-air SpO₂ average (typically 97%–99%).
03.limitations: Peripheral vasoconstriction, cold extremities, nail polish, or severe motion artifact distort pulse ox readings.
03.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & Vol 2, Sec. 6.2 (Cardiopulmonary & Respiratory Monitoring)

04.name: Blood Pressure Classification
how_to_measure: Rest seated/relaxed for 5 minutes; apply pneumatic cuff over bare upper arm aligned with brachial artery.
Support arm at heart level without muscle tension; initiate automated inflation cycle on monitor.
Remain still and silent during deflation; record systolic, diastolic, and MAP readings into health log.
04.what: Dynamic systemic arterial pressure (systolic, diastolic, mean arterial pressure).
04.why_space: Loss of gravity gradient alters central venous pressure and arterial baroreflex setpoint, precipitating post-landing and in-flight orthostatic instability.
04.space_effect: Central blood volume increases acutely before plasma volume contracts 10–15%; resting blood pressure remains normal or slightly decreased with reduced diurnal dipping.
04.abnormal: Hypotension poses syncope and cerebral hypoperfusion risks during G-transitions; hypertension exacerbates intracranial pressure and SANS progression.
04.baseline: 30-day pre-flight resting seated brachial blood pressure average.
04.limitations: Oscillometric cuffs sensitive to arm movement, improper cuff sizing, and microgravity arterial compliance shifts.
04.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Cardiovascular Standards & Hemodynamic Assessment)

05.name: Heart Rhythm
how_to_measure: Cleanse electrode sites with alcohol prep pads; apply pre-gelled Ag/AgCl telemetry electrodes.
Connect lead wires according to standard anatomical positions; power on ECG data acquisition unit.
Verify 12-lead signal baseline stability, check for motion artifact, and transmit rhythm strip to MCC.
05.what: Cardiac electrical conduction, sinus rhythm regularity, and cardiac ectopic activity.
05.why_space: Exposure to microgravity, electrolyte fluctuations (K+, Mg++), space radiation, and autonomic stress increases crew arrhythmogenic susceptibility.
05.normal_range: Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR), HR 60–100 bpm, < 1 PVC/hour
05.space_effect: Increased incidence of benign supraventricular and ventricular ectopy (PVCs, PACs) triggered by fluid shifts and elevated circulating catecholamines.
05.abnormal: Frequent or complex arrhythmias indicate myocardial irritability, electrolyte shifts, ischemia, or life-threatening conduction instability.
05.baseline: Pre-flight 24-hour Holter ECG recording documenting normal sinus rhythm and absence of complex ectopy.
05.limitations: Microgravity motion artifacts, dry gel electrode degradation, single-lead limitations in detecting complex ischemia.
05.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Cardiac Electrophysiology & Arrhythmia Monitoring)

06.name: Stand Test / Orthostatic Response
06.method: LBNP orthostatic challenge (in microgravity) / Active stand test (1g/planetary surface)
how_to_measure: Pre-test rest: 5 min supine. Microgravity: secure in LBNP device; Planetary/1g: lie supine before standing.
Microgravity: apply staged negative pressure (-10 to -40 mmHg LBNP); Planetary/1g: stand upright quietly with continuous HR/BP.
Maintain protocol for 3–5 min with continuous telemetry; log heart rate, blood pressure, and any presyncopal symptoms.
06.what: Baroreflex sensitivity, sympathetic vasoconstrictor reserve, and orthostatic tolerance.
06.why_space: Cardiovascular deconditioning and plasma volume loss in space impair cerebral perfusion upon re-exposure to gravity or during centrifuge operations.
06.normal_range: LBNP/Stand: HR increase < 20 bpm; SBP change between -10 and +10 mmHg
06.space_effect: Microgravity progressively degrades baroreflex sensitivity; astronauts exhibit excessive tachycardia and postural hypotension upon orthostatic stress.
06.abnormal: Exaggerated tachycardia or precipitous SBP drop indicates orthostatic intolerance, severe hypovolemia, and high presyncope risk.
06.baseline: Pre-flight standardized baseline LBNP response profile (-30 to -40 mmHg) and 10-minute active stand test.
06.limitations: Conventional stand test is impossible in free-floating microgravity; LBNP is required on orbit, while stand tests are reserved for 1g/planetary gravity.
06.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Orthostatic Intolerance & Neurovestibular Countermeasures)

07.name: Body Temperature
07.method: Infrared tympanic thermometer / ingestible core sensor pill
how_to_measure: Ensure sensor pill ingestion protocol or attach forehead double-sensor / inspect tympanic probe.
For tympanic: align ear canal and depress trigger for 1-second infrared scan; for sensor pill: hold receiver.
Confirm stable core temperature reading, log timestamp relative to circadian cycle and exercise.
07.what: Core body thermal balance, metabolic heat storage, and circadian thermoregulation.
07.why_space: Impaired convective and evaporative heat transfer in microgravity leads to sustained elevated core temperature ("space fever") and heat strain.
07.space_effect: Resting core body temperature resets approximately 1.0°C higher; thermoregulatory response during exercise is delayed with higher heat storage.
07.abnormal: Pyrexia indicates systemic infection, sepsis, or heat illness; hypothermia signals environmental ECLSS failure or severe metabolic collapse.
07.baseline: 14-day pre-flight circadian resting core temperature profile established across 24-hour cycles.
07.limitations: Tympanic readings operator-dependent; forehead heat-flux sensors impacted by local sweat layer; pill transit time variable.
07.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & Vol 2, Sec. 6.2.4 [V2 6012] (Thermoregulation & Clinical Monitoring)

08.name: Blood Glucose
08.method: Capillary fingerstick glucometer / minimally invasive CGM
how_to_measure: Cleanse finger puncture site with alcohol swab and allow skin to air dry completely.
Perform lancet puncture on lateral finger pad; wipe away first blood droplet and apply second droplet to strip.
Insert strip into calibrated POC glucometer; record fasting or 2-hour postprandial glucose value.
08.what: Peripheral glucose regulation, circulating glycemic levels, and insulin sensitivity.
08.why_space: Physical inactivity, dietary changes, and chronic stress in space induce insulin resistance and altered carbohydrate metabolism.
08.space_effect: Emergence of subclinical peripheral insulin resistance, elevated fasting insulin, and altered postprandial glycemic excursions.
08.abnormal: Hypoglycemia (<60 mg/dL) causes neuroglycopenia, cognitive impairment, and syncope; hyperglycemia (>180 mg/dL) indicates metabolic deregulation.
08.baseline: Pre-flight baseline fasting capillary glucose (average of 3 morning draws) and HbA1c.
08.limitations: Capillary fingerstick sampling sensitive to interstitial dilution and test strip moisture degradation in cabin air.
08.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.6 (Metabolic Profiling & Endocrine Function Monitoring)

09.name: Meals / Nutrition
09.method: Electronic food log (ISS FIT app) & barcode scanner
how_to_measure: Scan barcode of each food/beverage package using ISS FIT tablet scanner prior to consumption.
Enter portion percentage consumed (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and log additional water rehydration volume.
Submit daily dietary log to synchronize macronutrient, sodium, and caloric totals with Mission Control.
09.what: Daily caloric energy intake, fluid consumption, and macronutrient/micronutrient balance.
09.why_space: Anorexia of spaceflight and high operational tempo often result in chronic negative energy balance, accelerating muscle and bone degradation.
09.normal_range: Caloric intake: 2,500 – 3,200 kcal/day (crew-specific); Fluid intake: ≥ 2.5 L/day
09.space_effect: Voluntary caloric intake frequently drops to 70–80% of daily energy expenditure; fluid intake decreases due to blunted thirst reflex.
09.abnormal: Prolonged deficits cause rapid lean muscle wasting, exacerbated bone demineralization, immune dysfunction, and impaired operational endurance.
09.baseline: NASA nutritional prescription based on basal metabolic rate (BMR) and individual body mass.
09.limitations: Subject to crew recall bias, barcode scanning omissions, and estimation error of shared or uneaten food rations.
09.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.6 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.1 (Crew Nutrition & Food System Requirements)

10.name: Sleep
how_to_measure: Fasten Actiwatch device to non-dominant wrist and don dry-sensor sleep EEG headband before lights-out.
Press event marker button when attempting sleep and upon final morning awakening.
Dock devices into station laptop upon waking to offload sleep latency, duration, and architecture metrics.
10.what: Total sleep time (TST), sleep architecture (SWS/REM), and sleep efficiency.
10.why_space: 90-minute circadian orbital cycles, vehicle noise, and microgravity sleeping postures disrupt sleep architecture and induce cumulative sleep debt.
10.space_effect: Sleep duration decreases to 5.8–6.2 hours on orbit; slow-wave sleep (SWS) and REM sleep are reduced and fragmented.
10.abnormal: Chronic sleep restriction impairs cognitive function, psychomotor vigilance, decision-making, and emotional stability.
10.baseline: Pre-flight 14-day actigraphy and subjective sleep diary establishing individual baseline sleep duration.
10.limitations: Actigraphy overestimates sleep during quiet motionless wakefulness; EEG headbands prone to night displacement.
10.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.3 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.3 [V2 7038] (Sleep & Circadian Entrainment)

11.name: Mood
how_to_measure: Open computerized behavioral survey (B-CAT) on crew iPad during evening scheduled evaluation.
Rate subjective mood, interpersonal cohesion, operational stress, and perceived workload on visual scales.
Submit confidential response packet directly to Flight Surgeon / Behavioral Health Support link.
11.what: Psychological well-being, emotional stability, operational stress, and crew cohesion.
11.why_space: Prolonged confinement, isolation, heavy workloads, and sensory deprivation heighten vulnerability to mood disorders and interpersonal friction.
11.space_effect: Mood scores can fluctuate during mission mid-point ("third-quarter phenomenon") as psychological strain accumulates.
11.abnormal: Marked mood decrements signal psychological distress, operational burnout, anxiety, or depressive reaction requiring clinical intervention.
11.baseline: Pre-flight neurobehavioral evaluation baseline score across multiple standardized domains.
11.limitations: Self-report surveys subject to operational reporting bias, social desirability, and mission stigma concerns.
11.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.4 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.4 (Behavioral Health & Psychological Support)

12.name: Reaction Time
how_to_measure: Launch standardized 3-minute PVT-B software protocol on crew tablet in a quiet environment.
Respond as rapidly as possible to millisecond counter stimuli using dominant thumb press.
Review mean response speed (1/RT), fastest 10% RT, and lapse frequency (RT ≥ 355 ms); log automated test report.
12.what: Psychomotor speed, sustained attention, vigilance, and executive processing speed.
12.why_space: Cognitive slowing and lapse frequency directly threaten flight safety during complex maneuvers (docking, robotics, EVA).
12.normal_range: Mean RT: 200 – 250 ms; 0 – 1 lapses (≥355 ms) per 3-minute PVT-B trial
12.space_effect: Slower reaction times and increased attentional lapses occur primarily during high-workload phases, circadian desynchrony, and sleep deficit.
12.abnormal: Increased response latencies and lapses (>2) indicate critical cognitive fatigue, hypercapnic impairment, or acute sleep loss.
12.baseline: Pre-flight standardized 3-minute PVT-B baseline mean response speed (1/RT) and lapse frequency.
12.limitations: Validated for 3-minute duration using ≥355 ms lapse threshold (vs 500 ms in 10-min PVT); sensitive to acute caffeine, fatigue, or display latency.
12.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.4 & Vol 2, Sec. 10.1 (Cognitive Performance & Psychomotor Vigilance)

13.name: Exercise
13.method: CEVIS cycle ergometer, T2 treadmill & ARED telemetry
how_to_measure: Connect heart rate chest strap and calibrate exercise hardware telemetry (CEVIS / T2 / ARED).
Execute prescribed cardiovascular or resistive training protocol maintaining target heart rate/workload.
Offload exercise performance telemetry file (power wattage, speed, total force, work volume) to ground.
13.what: Cardiorespiratory work volume, aerobic power output, and resistive force generation.
13.why_space: Daily exercise countermeasures (CEVIS, T2, ARED) are essential to prevent severe musculoskeletal and cardiovascular deconditioning.
13.normal_range: Aerobic: ≥ 30 min/day at 70–85% HRmax; Resistive: prescribed ARED load sets (100% compliance)
13.space_effect: Exercise capacity (VO2peak) drops 15–20% without high-intensity training; mechanical loading must be artificially applied.
13.abnormal: Low compliance or falling power output directly accelerates muscle atrophy, bone mineral loss, and post-landing disability.
13.baseline: Pre-flight VO2max evaluation and 1-rep maximum (1RM) resistive loading profiles.
13.limitations: CEVIS and ARED telemetry measure mechanical load, not direct in-vivo muscle fiber tension or bone strain.
13.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.2 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.2 (Aerobic & Resistive Countermeasure Systems)

14.name: Bone Biomarkers
how_to_measure: Collect fasting venous/capillary blood sample into specified EDTA/heparin collection tube.
Centrifuge sample if required, load microfluidic analysis cartridge with plasma aliquot.
Run automated cartridge in onboard POC bioanalyzer; record bone turnover markers (CTX, P1NP, Ca++).
14.what: Systemic bone resorption (serum CTX) and formation (P1NP, osteocalcin) turnover rates.
14.why_space: Absence of weight-bearing loading induces severe uncoupling of bone remodeling, releasing skeletal calcium into circulation.
14.normal_range: Serum CTX: 0.15 – 0.55 ng/mL; Total Calcium: 8.5 – 10.2 mg/dL
14.space_effect: Bone resorption markers (CTX) increase by 50–100% within days, while bone formation markers remain flat or decrease.
14.abnormal: Accelerated resorption indicates rapid cancellous bone decay, increased fracture vulnerability, and high risk of renal calculi.
14.baseline: Pre-flight serum CTX and calcium panel drawn during baseline medical examination.
14.limitations: Circadian rhythm in bone resorption; in-flight microfluidic cartridges sensitive to bubble formation in zero-g.
14.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.2 (Musculoskeletal Health & Bone Density Loss Mitigation)

15.name: Immune Biomarkers
how_to_measure: Collect morning unstimulated saliva using Salivette swab or obtain capillary fingerstick sample.
Process sample in onboard centrifuge and insert test strip/cartridge into cytokine immunoassay reader.
Measure concentrations of target cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha) and viral DNA copies; sync with ground.
15.what: Pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta) and leukocyte distribution.
15.why_space: Spaceflight stressors (radiation, microgravity, sleep deprivation) suppress cell-mediated immunity and provoke latent virus reactivation.
15.normal_range: IL-6: < 5.0 pg/mL; TNF-alpha: < 8.0 pg/mL; Normal leukocyte differentials
15.space_effect: Persistent subclinical immune dysregulation with cytokine elevation, blunted T-cell function, and reactivation of EBV/VZV herpesviruses.
15.abnormal: Cytokine changes are nonspecific; they must be interpreted alongside clinical symptoms, physical examination, and other laboratory findings.
15.baseline: Pre-flight resting cytokine baseline and viral antibody titer panel.
15.limitations: Cytokine changes are nonspecific; affected by circadian rhythm, exercise, and minor stress; requires clinical and laboratory correlation.
15.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.7 (Immunological Dysregulation & Host Defense)

16.name: Radiation Dose
16.method: Crew Passive Dosimeter (CPD) & Active Personal Dosimeter (APD)
how_to_measure: Wear active personal dosimeter (APD) on operational flight suit continuously during duty hours.
Perform weekly optical/digital readout and dock APD with station radiation console.
Inspect passive dosimeter badge (CPD) position and verify real-time dose rate alarms (<1.0 mSv/day).
16.what: Ambient ionizing radiation exposure and absorbed equivalent dose from GCR and SPE.
16.why_space: Space radiation outside Earth's magnetosphere produces cumulative DNA double-strand breaks, cancer risks, and acute radiation sickness risk.
16.normal_range: Background in LEO: 0.3 – 0.8 mSv/day (< 1.0 mSv/day nominal); Career limit based on NASA Permissible Exposure Limits
16.space_effect: Continuous exposure to galactic cosmic rays (GCR) and episodic solar particle events (SPE), yielding daily doses 100x higher than Earth surface.
16.abnormal: Dose rates > 10 mSv/hr trigger operational storm shelter protocols; clinical ARS requires high total absorbed dose (>0.7 Gy), dose rate, and whole-body exposure.
16.baseline: Cumulative lifetime radiation exposure record maintained by NASA Radiation Health Officer.
16.limitations: Dosimeters measure physical dose/rate; clinical ARS depends on total absorbed dose, exposure duration, radiation characteristics, and body volume exposed.
16.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.8 [V1 4029] & Vol 2, Sec. 6.8 (Space Permissible Exposure Limits & ALARA)

17.name: Cabin CO₂
17.method: ECLSS Major Constituent Analyzer (MCA) & portable sensor
how_to_measure: Power on handheld/portable optical CO2 sensor or query station ECLSS MCA telemetry channel.
Take ambient ppCO2 readings at crew breathing height across multiple station modules/sleep cabins.
Verify local ppCO2 is below 2.0 mmHg; verify adequate ventilation flow and cabin fan operation.
17.what: Ambient spacecraft cabin partial pressure of carbon dioxide (ppCO2).
17.why_space: In microgravity, absence of natural thermal convection causes CO2 accumulation around crew heads, triggering headaches and visual impairment.
17.normal_range: Cabin ppCO2 < 2.0 mmHg (approx. < 2,600 ppm); nominal target < 1.5 mmHg
17.space_effect: CO2 levels in closed spacecraft cabins run significantly higher than terrestrial atmospheric levels (0.3 mmHg), fluctuating with crew activity and ECLSS cycling.
17.abnormal: Elevated ppCO2 (>2.0 mmHg) is associated with astronaut headaches and SANS symptoms; clinical toxicity and narcosis occur at much higher terrestrial levels.
17.baseline: Vehicle ECLSS baseline environmental limit specification (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2).
17.limitations: Localized air stagnation pockets in station modules may differ substantially from central ECLSS MCA sensor readings.
17.citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2, Sec. 6.2.3 [V2 6027] (Environmental Health - Cabin CO2 Limits)

data_source_types.Live: Measured by the app (finger PPG clip or the on-screen reaction test).
data_source_types.Manual: Typed in or answered by the crew (log, daily check).
data_source_types.Mission device: Read from a mission instrument or data feed (dosimeter, cabin air analyser, lab analyser).

Scope.handoff: Do not label clinical validated or safe for operational deployment.

Jion JSON schema.handoff: The exported JSON is a provisional schema; adapt exact field names after Jion provides interface.

Emergency recognition.handoff: No isolated PPG loss or video limp flag diagnoses cardiac arrest.

Collapse duration.handoff: Jion and medical lead must agree candidate detector threshold, false-positive policy, crew-alert behavior.

Collapse check-in.decision: Possible collapse. Are you okay? Please respond.
Collapse check-in.handoff: Crew alarm must not wait for response timer in an actual emergency.

Live red flag integration.handoff: Agree with Jian: validated pulse signal-loss handling, SpO2 signal check, HR/rhythm flags.

Medical kit.handoff: Never embed medications/doses/devices not actually onboard.

Microgravity CPR.decision: ER for initial BLS per 2020 aerospace guidelines
Microgravity CPR.handoff: Train rescuers; secure patient/rescuer; transition to restraint system, do not infer technique works identically across spacecraft.

Earth communication.handoff: Request flight surgeon immediately, but do not wait for Earth transmission/response to act on-board.

Data source type.handoff: Live/Manual/Simulation/Mission device; original spreadsheet mixes the categories.

FDA pulse oximetry.handoff: Assessment includes symptoms and signal quality; normal values do not rule out emergencies.

Mission CO2 standard.handoff: 2 mmHg provisional watch, >3 one-hour noncompliance, off-nominal action mission-defined.

Mood scale.handoff: Do not claim numeric 1–10 mood score clinically validated.

Protocol validation.handoff: These are educational flow examples adapted from terrestrial guidance.

Demo switches.handoff: No real clearance/decision automation until medical and engineering signoff.

switches._note: clinical_auto_alert_enabled = false: no automatic alerts from real sensor data (Measurement / Research mode). Demo mode alerts on simulated data only.
